title: Dharma at the lake
hook: one brother may live: Yudhishthira chooses Nakula, and the yaksha shows who he really is

segments.voice: Yesterday: dharma, the right way, hidden as if in a cave, and the wonder that we live as if we'll never die. Your line was dharma is hidden; walk where the great walked.

The questions are over, and the yaksha is satisfied. One of your brothers may live, he says. Choose. On the shore lie four of them. Bhima, whose strength the family leans on. Arjuna, the archer they'll need in any war to come. And the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva. Yudhishthira looks at them all, one by one, for a long moment. Then he names one, and the yaksha asks him why.
screen: `ONE BROTHER MAY LIVE.` → `FOUR ON THE SHORE.` → `CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: Let Nakula live, Yudhishthira says. Why him? Why not Bhima, so strong, or Arjuna, whom you all depend on? Yudhishthira answers: my father had two wives, Kunti and Madri. I am Kunti's son, and I'm alive. Let Madri have a living son too. He passes over the brothers who could win him a war, and chooses the one who keeps the family fair. The yaksha is delighted. Because you hold not being cruel higher than gain or pleasure, he says, let all four of your brothers live. And they stand up, as if from sleep. Then the stranger shows his face. He is Dharma himself, Yudhishthira's own father, and the deer that ran off with the fire-sticks was Dharma too. Here's the teaching, and it's one of the epic's biggest. The Sanskrit word is anrishamsya: not being cruel, keeping your heart open to the person a cold calculation would leave out. The Mahabharata ranks it among the highest dharma, and this is the moment that shows why Yudhishthira is called Dharmaraja, the king of dharma. Dharma here isn't a rulebook. It's the moment the clever move and the kind move split, and you take the kind one. Dharma grants him gifts: the fire-sticks back, a year in hiding where no one will know them, and a mind set on generosity, truth and self-discipline. Today the same choice comes small: who gets picked, who gets the bigger share, whose turn it is. Dharma's question isn't who helps me most. It's who would be left out.
screen: `LET NAKULA LIVE.` · `A LIVING SON FOR MADRI TOO.` · `THE YAKSHA IS DHARMA, HIS FATHER.` · `ANRISHAMSYA: NOT BEING CRUEL` · then, large: `ALL FOUR STAND UP.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a group you belong to, a family, a team, a circle of friends, and look for the person in it who is easiest to overlook, the one without a loud voice on their side. Hold them in mind the way Yudhishthira holds Madri's sons in mind, and with each breath wish them well. If you pray, you can bring them into your prayer.
Dharma, the god who stood at the lake all along, revealed at last as Yudhishthira's own father. A test by a lake that ends with a fair choice, and four brothers alive. Today's word.
Your line: dharma puts non-cruelty above gain. A living son for each mother, and four brothers standing. Day eight hundred six, done.

howItsDone: Yudhishthira's choice of Nakula comes after the last of the questions, and the revelation that the yaksha was Dharma closes the story of the lake.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the end of the episode of the Yaksha's questions: the choice of Nakula; the brothers restored; the yaksha revealed as Dharma; the boons

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Yudhishthira chooses Nakula; the yaksha asks why not Bhima or Arjuna; his reasoning about Kunti and Madri; the yaksha restores all four because he values harmlessness/fairness above profit.

Confirm Dharma's self-revelation as Yudhishthira's father, that he took the form of the deer, and the boons: the arani returned; the Pandavas unrecognized during the year in hiding; Yudhishthira's wish to conquer covetousness, folly and anger and to be devoted to charity, truth and asceticism.
'A father asking his son: do you know what dharma asks of you?' is an interpretive line, not the text's.
Ganguli has the yaksha's reason as Yudhishthira regarding harmlessness (or not being cruel) above profit/pleasure; 'fairness above advantage' is a paraphrase. Confirm.

Editor pass: the yaksha's stated reason now follows Ganguli (harmlessness above gain and pleasure) instead of 'fairness above advantage', in the teach, screen and fork reveal; Yudhishthira's own reasoning (a son for each mother) is still framed as fairness.
